paper.title_en: Experimental realization of a $\cos(2\varphi)$ transmon qubit
paper.abstract_en: Symmetry-based selection rules make some atomic states remarkably long-lived, a protection superconducting circuits usually lack. We report coherent control and single-shot readout of a 13.6 MHz $\cos 2\varphi$ qubit in the soft-transmon regime. It consists of an island shunted to ground through an interferometer of Josephson junctions and superinductances that favors tunneling of pairs of Cooper pairs, so that Cooper-pair parity symmetry protects the qubit from dielectric loss. We measure a qubit charge matrix element over 100 times smaller than that of the circuit's unprotected plasmon transition, placing the dielectric limit on the qubit lifetime above 10 ms. The measured $T_1 = 70\,μ$s is instead predicted, with no free parameters, by the $1/f$ flux noise in the interferometer loop that limits dephasing ($T_{2\mathrm{E}} = 2.5\,μ$s). This experiment demonstrates that Cooper-pair parity symmetry protects against the dielectric loss it targets, and that the remaining limit is the interferometer's sensitivity to flux noise, which larger superinductances are predicted to reduce without compromising protection.
